examples.en: They say everyone comes empty-handed and leaves empty-handed.
My grandfather told me not to be greedy, since we come and go empty-handed.

examples.ko: 돈을 많이 모아도 공수래공수거인데 뭐 하러 싸워요?
examples.en: Even if you save lots of money you leave empty-handed, so why fight?

examples.ko: 공수래공수거라는 말이 요즘 더 마음에 와닿아요.
examples.en: The saying about coming and going empty-handed resonates with me more these days.
After going to my friend's funeral, the saying about coming and going empty-handed came to mind.

examples.ko: 공수래공수거를 알면서도 다들 더 갖고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: Even though they know we come and go empty-handed, everyone wants to have more.

explain: 욕심을 버리라고 말할 때 어른들이 자주 쓰는 사자성어예요. 보통 '공수래공수거라고 하잖아요', '공수래공수거인데'처럼 문장 속에서 인용하듯 써요. 재산이나 욕심의 허무함을 말하는 분위기라서 가벼운 농담보다는 진지한 대화에 어울려요.

phrases.en: Life is come empty, return empty, so don't be too greedy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인생 전체를 말하며 욕심을 내려놓으라고 조언할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to advise letting go of greed, speaking of life as a whole.
phrases.en_equiv: life is come empty, go empty

phrases.en: We come and go empty-handed, so let's live comfortably.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하는 연결형이라서 충고나 위로 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A reason-giving connective, placed before advice or comfort.
phrases.en_equiv: since we come and go empty-handed

phrases.en: The elders say we come and go empty-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른들의 말을 인용해서 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to quote what elders say.
phrases.en_equiv: they say come empty, go empty

explain_en: It is a four-character saying that older people often use when telling someone to let go of greed. It is typically quoted within a sentence, as in '공수래공수거라고 하잖아요' or '공수래공수거인데'. It talks about the emptiness of wealth and desire, so it suits serious conversation more than light jokes.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 별을 보고 날씨를 예언하려고 했어요.
examples.en: In the old days, people tried to predict the weather by looking at the stars.

examples.ko: 그는 경제가 곧 나빠질 거라고 예언하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is predicting that the economy will soon get worse.

examples.ko: 미래를 예언하는 사람은 많지만 맞히는 사람은 드물어요.
examples.en: Many people predict the future, but few get it right.

examples.ko: 책 속 마법사가 왕의 죽음을 예언해요.
examples.en: The wizard in the book foretells the king's death.

examples.ko: 아무도 그런 일이 생길 거라고 예언할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Nobody could have predicted that such a thing would happen.

examples.ko: 누가 내일 일을 예언하면 정말 믿을 수 있겠어요?
examples.en: If someone foretold tomorrow's events, could you really believe it?

explain: 예언은 신비한 힘이나 종교적인 느낌이 있어요. 자료를 보고 미리 계산할 때는 '예측하다', 뉴스에서 앞날을 내다볼 때는 '전망하다'를 써요. 날씨나 경기 결과에는 '예언'보다 '예상'이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: That person's prediction turned out to be right.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a prediction turns out to be true.

phrases.example: 옛 이야기에는 앞날을 보는 예언자가 나와요.
phrases.en: Old stories feature a prophet who sees the future.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예언하는 사람을 말하며 신비한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who prophesies, with a mystical feel.

phrases.nuance_ko: 자료를 보고 미리 계산할 때는 '예언하다' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of 예언하다 when predicting from data.

explain_en: 예언하다 carries a mystical or religious feel. When you calculate ahead from data, use 예측하다; in news about the outlook, 전망하다. For weather or match results, 예상 is more natural than 예언.

examples.en: He raised his hand without hesitation.
There was no time to hesitate, so I dove right in.

examples.ko: 잠깐의 주저 끝에 그는 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: After a moment's hesitation, he opened the door.
I could sense hesitation in her voice.
Don't hesitate to ask whatever you're curious about.
I hesitated a lot before making the decision.

explain: '주저 없이', '주저하지 말고'처럼 거의 정해진 모양으로 많이 써요. 특히 '주저하지 말고 연락 주세요'는 편지나 안내문에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 자주 나와요. 말로는 '망설이지 말고'가 더 부드러워요.

phrases.example: 그는 질문을 듣고 주저 없이 대답했어요.
phrases.en: He answered without hesitation after hearing the question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 망설임 없이 바로 하는 모습을 말하는 가장 흔한 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common set form for doing something right away.

phrases.example: 궁금한 게 있으면 주저하지 말고 물어보세요.
phrases.en: If you're curious about anything, don't hesitate to ask.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 이메일에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used politely in notices and emails.

phrases.en: There was no hesitation in her voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주저'보다 말할 때 더 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more everyday word than 주저.

explain_en: It mostly appears in set patterns like 주저 없이 and 주저하지 말고. 주저하지 말고 연락 주세요 is a very common polite line in letters and notices. In speech, 망설이지 말고 sounds softer.

examples.en: I have mixed feelings after hearing my friend's news.
With graduation coming up, my feelings are all mixed.
He looked out the window with a troubled expression.
I was both happy and sad, so my heart was in a tangle.

examples.ko: 이사하는 날 빈 집을 보니 착잡하더라고요.
examples.en: On moving day, seeing the empty house left me with mixed feelings.

examples.ko: 마음이 착잡해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: My feelings were so tangled that I couldn't say anything.

explain: 기쁨과 슬픔, 걱정이 한꺼번에 섞여 마음이 복잡하고 무거울 때 써요. '복잡하다'보다 감정이 무겁고 쓸쓸한 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '마음이/기분이 착잡하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I came home with mixed feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '착잡하다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 마음 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun to describe one's state of mind.

phrases.en: For some reason my heart feels heavy and mixed today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금의 기분을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form for describing how you feel now.

phrases.en: He read the letter with a conflicted look on his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하지 않아도 복잡한 감정이 얼굴에 드러날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when mixed feelings show on someone's face.

explain_en: Use it when joy, sadness and worry are mixed together and your heart feels heavy and tangled. Compared with '복잡하다', it carries a stronger sense of heaviness and loneliness. It is usually used as '마음이/기분이 착잡하다'.

en: to be expressed; to be represented; to be manifested

examples.en: That feeling is well expressed in the song.
Sadness was expressed in the painting.
This word is hard to express in English.
The season depicted in the poem is autumn.
Emotions show up on the face as they are.

examples.ko: 숫자로 표현될 수 없는 가치도 있어요.
examples.en: There are also values that can't be expressed in numbers.

explain: 감정이나 생각이 말, 그림, 얼굴 등으로 드러난다는 말이에요. '표현하다'는 내가 나타내는 것이고, '표현되다'는 감정이 주어로 나와요. 어디에 나타나는지는 '에/으로'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The sadness is well expressed in the painting.
phrases.nuance_en: Says thoughts or feelings come across well.

phrases.en: I can feel the feelings expressed in the writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드러난 감정이나 생각을 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for a feeling or thought that has been expressed.

phrases.en: My gratitude can't be put into words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로 다 나타낼 수 없는 감정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for feelings too big to put into words.

explain_en: It means a feeling or thought shows through words, pictures or a face. '표현하다' has you expressing something, while with 표현되다 the feeling itself is the subject. '에' or '(으)로' marks where it appears.

dis.h: be expressed in words, art, or looks

p.n: 표출되다 stresses emotion bursting outward; 표현되다 is neutral.

en: to be futile; to be empty

examples.en: I feel empty because the exam I prepared so hard for was canceled.
Feeling hollow, I just looked at the sky for a long time.
The match ended so easily that it was anticlimactic.
All the effort vanished into nothing.

examples.ko: 일이 끝나고 나니 허무하다는 생각이 들었어요.
examples.en: After the work was over, I felt a sense of emptiness.
I set small goals so I wouldn't feel empty.

explain: 열심히 했는데 결과가 없거나, 기대한 것이 갑자기 사라졌을 때의 힘 빠진 마음이에요. 비슷한 '허탈하다'는 몸에 힘이 쭉 빠지는 느낌이고, '허무하다'는 모든 것이 의미 없어진 것 같은 느낌이 더 커요. '허무하게 끝나다', '허무하게 지다'처럼 부사형으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 오랫동안 준비한 일이 취소돼서 허무한 기분이 들었어요.
phrases.en: I felt empty because something I had prepared for a long time was canceled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허무한'이 명사 '기분'을 꾸미는 쓰임으로, 감정을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing the noun 기분, used often to explain a feeling.

phrases.en: The game I was looking forward to ended anticlimactically.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대에 비해 결과가 너무 빨리, 쉽게 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something ends too quickly or easily compared to expectations.

phrases.example: 열심히 만든 파일이 지워져서 너무 허무했어요.
phrases.en: I felt so empty because the file I worked hard on was deleted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 해요체로, 이미 지나간 일에 힘이 빠진 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past polite form, expressing deflation over something that already happened.

explain_en: It describes the deflated feeling when hard work leads to nothing or something you expected suddenly disappears. The similar '허탈하다' is more about strength draining out of you, while '허무하다' leans toward a feeling that everything has become meaningless. The adverb form is common too, as in '허무하게 끝나다' and '허무하게 지다'.
